what: TransDigm makes small, highly engineered aircraft parts: pumps, valves, latches, ignition systems and cockpit controls. Most are sole-source designs on aircraft already flying, so it sells replacements at high margins for decades.
customers: Aircraft and engine manufacturers, airlines, repair shops and defence customers worldwide.
money: pumps, valves, ignition systems and actuators
latches, seating components, cockpit and cabin parts
moat: Parts that are sole-source and certified onto an aircraft type; an airline cannot buy them elsewhere without recertifying the aircraft.
risks: Debt of about $34 billion is extremely high, used to fund buyouts and special dividends
Airlines and regulators have criticised its pricing on sole-source parts
A downturn in air travel cuts the aftermarket demand that drives profit
It depends on continuing acquisitions to grow
opportunities: Operating margin near 46% is among the highest in any manufacturing industry
Record flight hours drive the spare parts demand that is most of its profit
Defence aftermarket adds a second demand source
watch: Aftermarket revenue growth and the leverage ratio against earnings.
